name: Macrospin magnetic tunnel junction with a perpendicular reference layer, reduced to m_z
question: Which functions of the history of the input voltage does the junction resistance represent?

provenance.source: Furuta, Fujii, Nakajima, Tsunegi, Kubota, Suzuki and Miwa, Phys. Rev. Applied 10, 034063 (2018), arXiv:1805.09977, Eqs. (12)-(16) and Table I; reduced to m_z with the corrections listed in model_sheet.md section 3c

assumptions: the standard dissipative Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equation in place of the printed Eq. (12) (sign of the precession term and the missing division by the angular momentum of the layer)
Eq. (16) with the factor 2 that gives R = R_P and R_AP at the parallel and antiparallel states
spin polarization P = 0.548 from Julliere's relation (not stated in the source); it reproduces the source's +-44 mV
gyromagnetic ratio 1.76e11 rad/(s T) (not stated in the source)
axial symmetry: R depends on m_z alone, so the azimuth is a mode hidden from the observable and the body reduces to m_z
time in ns, Vin in mV, R in ohm; no thermal fluctuations (as in the source)

drift.mz: (1 - mz**2)*(-kJ*P/(1 + P**2*mz)*Vin/(2*RAP*RP/((RAP + RP) + (RAP - RP)*mz)) - damp*mz)/(1 + alpha**2)
